The shahi baaja is an Indian chordophone, an electrified adaptation of the Indian bulbul tarang (a zither), fitted with typewriter keys and a ten-string drone harp. The body is about 94 cm long, of solid wood, with two pickups, tone and volume controls and 30 keys; two main strings, three sympathetic strings and ten drone strings. The player plucks or strums with a pick and the keys change the pitch of the melody strings; the drone and sympathetic strings are fretless. It is used in semi-classical, pop, ambient techno, psychedelic rock, indie and fusion music, and also in film music and in the devotional songs of the north Indian stage, Sufi music and ghazal; a few musicians have tried it in Indian classical music.
沙希巴傑琴源自印度 bulbul tarang，經加裝打字機鍵與十條無品弦，成為: The shahi baaja comes from the Indian bulbul tarang; with typewriter keys and ten fretless strings added it became an electrified, pickup-equipped version of the zither. Its important changes include two pickups, tone and volume controls, thirty keys and a solid wood body. In its development it moved from semi-classical and popular Indian music into ambient techno, psychedelic rock, indie and fusion music; at least forty major bands use it as a lead instrument or to accompany vocals, among them Twigs, Beck and Rapoon. Since 2006 Michael Flower and Chris Corsano have played it as a free improvisation duo. Several Indian music directors have also used it for film music, and on the north Indian stage it is used for bhajan, Sufi music and ghazal.
沙希巴傑琴現見於印度半古典與流行音樂，也進入環境科技音樂、迷幻搖滾、獨立音樂與融: The shahi baaja now appears in Indian semi-classical and popular music, and has also entered ambient techno, psychedelic rock, indie and fusion music, as a lead instrument or accompanying vocals. At least forty major bands use it, and several Indian music directors use it in film music; on the north Indian stage it appears in bhajan, Sufi music and ghazal. Other players have tried it in Indian classical music, and it is also heard in free improvisation duos.
沙希巴傑琴音色兼具現代感與傳統韻味，具有明亮且穿透力強的特質。其電子化改良使音色: The shahi baaja's timbre is both modern and traditional, bright and strongly carrying. The electronic modification gives it a metallic edge while keeping the warm, elegant base of the original bulbul tarang. Its range is wide, from a deep, heavy low register to a clear, high top. The typewriter key mechanism gives it a particular mechanical feel, producing an effect like a harp and a piano combined. The ten fretless strings add layers of resonance, so the tone has both the softness of strings and the modernity of electronic music. Compared with a traditional harp it carries more; compared with an electric guitar it sounds gentler. These qualities let it interpret styles from classical to avant-garde.
